message.content:
This appears to be a CBP ruling on a Hypertherm receptacle subassembly (wiring harness) for a plasma arc cutting machine. Candidate headings are 8544.42 (insulated electric conductors fitted with connectors, for voltage ≤1,000 V), 8544.49, and 8515.90 (parts of plasma arc cutting machines).

The harness is a set of insulated copper conductors with connectors at each end, so 8544.42.90 is the natural fit. Section XVI Note 2 sends parts to a machine's heading only when they are not goods of a general-purpose heading such as 8544. Because 8544 covers the harness, it is excluded from 8515.90. Wiring harnesses are therefore classified in 8544.

For 8544.42.9090, the current HTS breaks out as follows:
- 8544.42.20 covers conductors fitted with connectors, for telecommunications.
- 8544.42.90 covers other conductors, with a 10-digit statistical suffix.

The current 8544.42.90 subdivisions are 8544.42.9010 (insulated, with connectors, ≤1,000 V; tied to certain uses) and 8544.42.9090 (other). I am fairly confident the "other" line is 8544.42.9090, though I am not certain of the suffix.

```json
{"hts_code": "8544.42.9090", "reason": "A wiring harness of insulated copper conductors fitted with connectors at each end, for voltage not over 1,000 V, is classified in heading 8544 (insulated wire/cable with connectors), which takes precedence over parts of welding/cutting machines under Section XVI Note 2."}
```
